req.title: Reject negative squadNumber
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 422 when squadNumber is not a positive integer.

doc.reasoning: R-PLAYER-023 requires HTTP 422 when squadNumber is not a positive integer. The violation was test[4] having kind=negative but heuristic=EP. The rule requires that negative-kind tests use heuristic=NEG (not EP). Fix: change test[4] (test_post_player_large_negative_squad_number_returns_422) from heuristic=EP to heuristic=NEG, since it is a negative test exercising an invalid input partition. All other tests are preserved exactly as they were. The heuristic EP is reserved for positive equivalence partition tests; NEG is the correct heuristic for negative tests that exercise invalid input classes.

tests.name: test_post_player_valid_positive_squad_number_returns_201
preconditions: App is running in-process via TestClient
Database contains pre-loaded rows with squadNumbers 1-26
squadNumber 99 does not exist in the pre-loaded dataset
actions: POST /players/ with a valid payload where squadNumber=99 (a positive integer not in the pre-loaded set)
expected: Response body contains squadNumber equal to 99
Response body contains firstName equal to the submitted value
trace: R-PLAYER-023: positive integer squadNumber must be accepted (HTTP 2xx)
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
client = TestClient(app)

payload = {
    "firstName": "Test",
    "lastName": "Player",
    "squadNumber": 99,
    "position": "Goalkeeper"
}
r = client.post("/players/", json=payload)
assert r.status_code == 201
body = r.json()
assert body["squadNumber"] == 99
assert body["firstName"] == "Test"
assert body["lastName"] == "Player"
assert body["position"] == "Goalkeeper"

tests.name: test_post_player_squad_number_one_returns_201_boundary_minimum_positive
preconditions: App is running in-process via TestClient
squadNumber=1 already exists in the pre-loaded dataset (Anjali Banerjee)
squadNumber=1 is the smallest positive integer
actions: POST /players/ with squadNumber=1 (already exists in DB)
expected: HTTP 409 Conflict (not 422), confirming the value 1 passed validation and reached the duplicate-check logic
trace: R-PLAYER-023: squadNumber=1 is the minimum positive integer and must pass validation (not return 422)
BVA: one is the exact lower boundary of valid positive integers; a 422 here would indicate an off-by-one error in the validator
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
client = TestClient(app)

payload = {
    "firstName": "Boundary",
    "lastName": "Player",
    "squadNumber": 1,
    "position": "Goalkeeper"
}
r = client.post("/players/", json=payload)
assert r.status_code == 409
assert r.status_code != 422

tests.name: test_post_player_squad_number_minus_one_vs_plus_one_boundary_comparison
preconditions: App is running in-process via TestClient
squadNumber=27 does not exist in the pre-loaded dataset (valid)
expected: The two status codes are different, confirming the boundary is correctly placed
trace: R-PLAYER-023: BVA ±1 around the positive boundary; catches operator-flip mutations (> vs >=, < vs <=)
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
client = TestClient(app)

bad_payload = {
    "firstName": "Neg",
    "lastName": "One",
    "squadNumber": -1,
    "position": "Goalkeeper"
}
r_bad = client.post("/players/", json=bad_payload)
assert r_bad.status_code == 422

good_payload = {
    "firstName": "Pos",
    "lastName": "TwentySeven",
    "squadNumber": 27,
    "position": "Goalkeeper"
}
r_good = client.post("/players/", json=good_payload)
assert r_good.status_code == 201
assert r_good.json()["squadNumber"] == 27
